items.title: Saudi Arabia says it downed three Houthi ballistic missiles Monday
items.summary: Saudi Arabia said it intercepted and destroyed three Houthi ballistic missiles on Monday — one over Riyadh and two over Khamis Mushait in the southwest. The Houthis claimed responsibility, saying they targeted King Khalid International Airport and a military base, and renewed warnings to airlines against flying to Saudi airports. The week's Houthi attacks have killed at least 20 people and wounded hundreds, per CNN's tally.

items.title: Saudi cuts oil shipments to European refineries after pipeline damage; UK sends advisers
items.summary: Saudi Arabia has cut some oil shipments to key European refineries after drone attacks damaged its key export pipeline, The Times reports — stoking European supply-shock fears, with diesel expected to top £2 a litre in the UK. Separately, PM Andy Burnham agreed Monday evening to RAF Voyager defensive air-to-air refuelling for Saudi jets, with a small team of British military advisers deployed to the kingdom and support beginning within days (expanding the refuelling mission first announced in September).

items.title: USS Theodore Roosevelt moves in; three US carrier groups now near region
items.summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt is approaching the region, temporarily bringing three US aircraft carrier battle groups to the area, RANE reports — the biggest US naval concentration there in months. It lands as Trump weighs joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis and MBS lobbies him for action, and as analysts warn Riyadh could be pushed toward ground operations in Yemen.
